answer: A hardware-rooted attestation protocol requires each agent to anchor its keypairs in a tamper-proof walnut security module before entering the validation oasis. An attacker incurs a verifiable marginal cost in dedicated silicon dies and power infrastructure for every synthesized identity. Each identity must also mature across a glacier timelock before accessing network liquidity. However, this model discriminates against purely virtualized agents and remains susceptible to physical supply-chain exploits.
